title: Azure Bicep - Simply Explained

entities.name: Infrastructure as code
entities.quote: That idea has a name. Infrastructure as code, and the name makes it sound heavier than it really is.

entities.name: Bicep
entities.quote: Azure bicep exists to change that.

entities.name: Microsoft Azure
entities.quote: Your Azure setup lives in your memory and that's a problem.

entities.name: Terraform
entities.quote: By now, you've probably heard a third name in the same breath as bicep, and that name is Terraform.

quotes.text: The portal isn't the problem here. It's a good place to look at what you already have. It's a poor place to keep the definition of what you have, because that definition is a memory and memories fade.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why clicked configuration needs to be written down.

quotes.text: You don't tell Azure to click here, then there, then somewhere else, and you don't have to guess the right order of steps. You write down the end state you want, and Azure works out the order of operations on its own.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A crisp definition of declarative infrastructure.

quotes.text: Bicep is the language and ARM is the engine underneath it. That matters because you aren't choosing between something new and something old. You're choosing a cleaner way to write the exact same instructions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the relationship between Bicep and ARM.

quotes.text: Previewing a change before it goes live is what separates a calm rollout from a frantic one, and it costs you nothing but the few seconds it takes to read the output.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for always running what-if before deploying.

quotes.text: Write anything new in bicep and convert the old files only when you have a reason to touch them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical migration advice for teams with existing ARM templates.

chapters.title: Why not ARM JSON or the portal
How Bicep works under the hood

takeaways: Bicep is a declarative, readable language for Azure infrastructure that compiles to ARM JSON, with Azure Resource Manager doing the deployment.
Parameters, decorators, symbolic names and modules keep Bicep files reusable, while dependencies are mostly worked out automatically.
Run what-if before every deployment, and choose Bicep for Azure-only work or Terraform when you span several clouds.
hook: Many Azure environments exist only as a memory of portal clicks that nobody wrote down. This episode explains Azure Bicep for admins and beginners who are not developers, from parameters and modules to what-if previews. You will learn how to turn your Azure setup into a readable file you can review, share and redeploy.
